title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation

details.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
details.abstract: We introduce Wave Forcing, a training and execution framework for streaming video generation. The key idea is wavefront scheduling: later video chunks begin denoising before earlier chunks finish, using their cleaner intermediate states as causal context. WaveRT sends K/V ahead of use and overlaps communication with computation. After pipeline fill, each concurrent forward round produces one video chunk. Key results: • Quality: On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing. For 100-second videos, Dynamic Degree improves from 36.63 to 91.45 and Subject Preservation from 92.75 to 97.10. • System efficiency: Our 4-step benchmark on 8×H200 reaches 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS, delivering 7.07× single-GPU E2E throughput.å • Parallelism: Up to 2.53× the throughput of the faster Ulysses/Ring baseline in DiT-only tests with  matched SageAttention+W8A8 backends, step counts and GPU counts. Code, training recipes, and 4-step/5-step checkpoints are available. We welcome feedback and discussion! Project page: https://sjtu-deng-lab.github.io/WaveForcing/ GitHub repo: https://github.com/SJTU-DENG-Lab/WaveForcing

title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement

details.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
details.abstract: Video generation is evolving from end-to-end synthesis toward agentic systems that integrate planning, tool use, and feedback. Meanwhile, video world models are enabling interactive, action-conditioned environments for agents. In this survey, we explore their intersection through the lens of the  agent harness , an executable runtime that manages tools, context, state, feedback, and budgets around video models. We focus on three areas: Agentic Video Generation: Multi-shot planning, production, editing, and evaluation. Agentic World Modeling: Interactive observation, control, and state management. Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI): Improving video outputs, harnesses, models, and the improvement process itself. We also discuss essential agent capabilities and open challenges toward autonomous video production and self-improving video systems. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40191 🌐 Homepage: https://agentic-videogen.github.io/ 💻 Github: https://github.com/agentic-videogen/awesome-agentic-videogen

title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models

details.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
details.abstract: We introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for robot-use agents with open-weight models, designed to support further training. Without privileged inputs, out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, exceeding the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe result of 28.97, while also performing competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Beyond benchmarking, we systematically analyze models across generations, families, and sizes, identifying four general capabilities linked to effective robot use. Our findings suggest that future robot-use agent training should develop these capabilities jointly.

title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings

details.title: From Fragmentation to Fusion: A Survey and Roadmap for Omnimodal Embeddings
details.abstract: Despite shared mathematical foundations, embedding research across text, vision, audio, graphs, tables, and time series remains largely fragmented into modality-specific silos. This survey and position paper argues that embedding research is quietly converging around universal principles: contrastive learning objectives, Transformer backbones, the pretrain–finetune recipe, and an upward shift toward whole semantic units. To evaluate progress toward true unification, we introduce the 3C framework—Coverage, Comparability, and Compositionality—which maps onto three progressive paths: format transformation, cross-modal alignment, and deep joint fusion, our advocated terminus that subsumes alignment and eliminates the modality gap. Reaching this goal will require preserving unique modality-specific structures, cross-pollinating techniques across research communities, and building unified benchmarks that measure true compositional gains.

title: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers

details.title: DeFT-RAG: Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
details.abstract: DeFT-RAG asks a different question about multi-hop RAG: instead of planning all sub-questions and their dependencies in advance, what if the LLM writes just one self-contained sub-question at a time? Each sub-question names every entity it asks about, so it never has to be rewritten, and its answer stays correct for any question that asks it. The rest of the work moves outside the LLM: a QA table updated by rules keeps track of what is known, and a fine-tuned 4B decision model makes the yes/no decisions and estimates question depth. A QA cache reuses answers across questions. On MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA, DeFT-RAG achieves the best accuracy among 13 baselines with both gpt-4o-mini and Qwen3.6, including +5.2 points on MuSiQue over Hi-Q, while giving the LLM fewer input tokens than any other iterative method. With a shared QA cache, 23.1% of sub-questions are answered from the cache, reducing LLM calls by 12.9% without lowering accuracy. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37826 💻 Code: https://github.com/Dingyi-Kang/DeFT-RAG 🤗 Decision model: https://huggingface.co/Dingy-Kang/DeFT-RAG-DM-4B

title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers

details.title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
details.abstract: Decision models target structured tasks by directly predicting choices or scores, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency. However, transferring a generative LLM's ranking knowledge to a decision model remains challenging: the teacher expresses preferences through a ranked list of document ID sequences, while the student determines the ranking using scores from the first-token position. To bridge this gap, we introduce DecisionRank, a decision model trained through item-space on-policy distillation (OPD). Item-space OPD constructs the student's rollout by sorting its document scores into a ranked sequence. A generative teacher takes the resulting ranking list as inputs and provides conditional feedback to directly supervise those scores. Combined with offline ranking supervision, DecisionRank achieves state-of-the-art performance on both general and reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmarks such as TREC DL, BEIR, and BRIGHT. Across four benchmarks, item-space OPD consistently outperforms alternative training objectives. Even at 1.7B parameters, DecisionRank surpasses its 27B generative teacher on TREC DL19-23. At 8B, it outperforms its generative listwise counterpart while running 24.5× faster on TREC DL and 16.7× faster on BRIGHT.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents

details.title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
details.abstract: TinyAstral evolves the harness (tools, feedback, memory, recovery) of a frozen ~180B robot teacher through recursive self-improvement (33.4% → 63.6% on RoboTwin), then distills it into 0.8B–4B students that run in the same harness. The 4B student stays close to its teacher on six manipulation benchmarks at about one fifth of the compute, and runs closed loop on a real arm. Code, weights and data are released.

title: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads

details.title: MAServeBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent LLM Serving Systems with Hierarchical Collaboration Workloads
details.abstract: Multi-agent collaboration fundamentally reshapes LLM serving workloads through dynamic dependencies, synchronization, and context sharing—beyond what conventional request-level benchmarks can capture. We introduce MAServeBench , a benchmark featuring composable hierarchical collaboration patterns and dependency-preserving Semantic Traces for reproducible serving evaluation and architecture simulation. Our GPU/NPU studies reveal how collaboration affects compute efficiency, KV cache pressure, and end-to-end task performance. We hope this work helps guide the design of next-generation serving systems and hardware for agentic AI. Feedback and discussions are very welcome!

details.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Teacher Evolution
details.abstract: We wanted to solve a frustrating problem in On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD): the "self-teacher" model often gets blinded by the privileged context and gives pretty unreliable, overconfident token-level guidance, which ends up misleading the student model. To fix this, we proposed TESD (Teacher-Evolution Self-Distillation): We let the teacher evolve dynamically by optimizing it with environment feedback. We automatically down-weight those training samples where the teacher's guidance is deemed unreliable. As a result, TESD consistently beats standard token-level distillation (like SDPO) and even sequence-level RL (like GRPO) across benchmarks like SciKnowEval and Tooluse.

details.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
details.abstract: Speculative decoding lets a small model draft and a large model verify. ProVe reverses the roles: the large model proposes a block of 16 tokens in one forward pass, and a verifier reads it in one more.
